title: Demand Response Programs Device Operating Limits During Events
content:
**Operating limits.** When the company operates a customer's thermostat, air conditioning switch or home battery during an event under the Demand Response Programs, it stays within the limits below. A limit of 0 means that the program does not operate that kind of device.

| Program | Battery capacity kept in reserve during dispatch | Largest thermostat setpoint change in an event | Share of each half-hour the compressor is switched off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Peak Time Rebate | 0.00 (not a battery program) | 0 °F (not a thermostat program) | 0.00 (not a cycling program) |
| Smart Thermostat Rewards | 0.00 (not a battery program) | 4 °F | 0.00 (not a cycling program) |
| AC Cycling Program | 0.00 (not a battery program) | 0 °F (not a thermostat program) | 0.50 — 50 percent of each half-hour |
| Home Battery Dispatch | 0.20 — 20 percent of capacity | 0 °F (not a thermostat program) | 0.00 (not a cycling program) |
| Commercial Capacity Bidding Program | 0.00 (not a battery program) | 0 °F (not a thermostat program) | 0.00 (not a cycling program) |
| Base Interruptible Program | 0.00 (not a battery program) | 0 °F (not a thermostat program) | 0.00 (not a cycling program) |

**The three operated devices in practice (hypothetical households)**

- *Smart Thermostat Rewards.* A thermostat set at 74 °F before an event may be moved to at most 78 °F during the event, a change of 4 °F.
- *AC Cycling Program.* The compressor is switched off for 50 percent of each half-hour: 15 minutes in every 30-minute period of the event.
- *Home Battery Dispatch.* A battery with 13.5 kWh of capacity keeps 20 percent of it, 2.7 kWh, in reserve; dispatch never draws it below that level.

The Peak Time Rebate, Commercial Capacity Bidding Program and Base Interruptible Program operate none of these devices.
